title: GP0 Global Graph search persistence comparison

matchedBehavior: The exact query is visible and applied at Global Graph entry.
The exact query remains visible and applied after Graph is closed and reopened.
The exact query remains visible and applied after a full application restart followed by Graph view.
notEstablished: Pixel parity between Obsidian and TSUZUNE.
Automatic restoration of the Graph workspace or Graph view at application startup.
Parity for other queries, filters, camera state, layout, animation, or Graph behaviors.

normalizedTopology.normalizationNote: The Obsidian probe reports renderedLinkCount 2 at each checkpoint while the screenshots show one visible connection between the only two rendered nodes. This comparison therefore uses one unique visible edge; TSUZUNE reports edgeCount 1 directly.

checkpoints.label: Query entry
checkpoints.condition: Global Graph after entering the exact query

checkpoints.label: Graph close and reopen
checkpoints.condition: Graph view after leaving it and opening it again in the same application process

checkpoints.label: Full application restart, then Graph view
checkpoints.condition: A second application process with Graph available for observation
checkpoints.limitation: This checkpoint does not establish automatic Graph workspace or view restoration at startup.

conclusion: For path:"10_projects" only, TSUZUNE matches the observed Obsidian 1.13.4 query-persistence behavior at entry, after Graph close/reopen, and after a full application restart followed by Graph view. The filtered topology remains two nodes and one unique visible edge at all three checkpoints.
